name: BEEGND-1
description:
### Station BEEGND-1

**B**erlin **E**xperimental and **E**ducational **G**rou**nd** Stations (**BEEGND**) are a series of stations built as part of a teaching project at [Technische Universität Berlin (TUB)](https://www.tu.berlin/).

BEEGND-1 is a fixed-antenna station in a remote, low-noise location (Hoher Fläming) about 80 km Southwest of Berlin. It comprises of two fixed-direction UHF Turnstile Antennas, SAW-Filters and a custom built [LNA-Filter-Board](https://git.dk0tu.de/afutub/famp-pcb/-/tree/rev3) and an Ettus B210-mini SDR.

The station enables observations in the UHF-Amateur (~435MHz) and in the UHF-Commercial (~400MHz) Band. It was build as part of TUBs [BEECON-Project](https://www.tu.berlin/en/raumfahrttechnik/research/current-projects/beecon), which develops a standardised satellite identification and tracking solution to improve Space Situational Awareness.

#### Quick Notes on Operations

Please mind some short remarks on the stations operation:

- The station uses fixed turnstile antennas. Thus, low-elevation passes will most certainly not perform well. The antennas work best at an elevation above 20 to 25 degrees.
- The station provides IQ-Data automatically. These can be loaded from: [https://tubcloud.tu-berlin.de/s/DkiRJ9jyLKRBmXE](https://tubcloud.tu-berlin.de/s/DkiRJ9jyLKRBmXE). The IQ-Data comes directly from the satnogs-flowgraph. It is doppler-corrected by the observations TLE. Please mind, that we will keep the data only for a limited time due to memory constraints.
- On this station we run a patched satnogs-client. It supports using both antenna ports of the Ettus SDR and chooses the right port based on the frequency requested in the observation

We are looking forward to see good observations. :)

name: BEEGND-4
description:
### Station BEEGND-4

**B**erlin **E**xperimental and **E**ducational **G**rou**nd** Stations (**BEEGND**) are a series of stations built as part of a teaching project at [Technische Universität Berlin](https://www.tu.berlin/).

[BEEGND-4](https://dk0tu.de/groundstation/) is hosted by TUB's Amateur Radio Club [AFuTUB](https://dk0tu.de). It comprises of an 4-Part Yagi Antenna Array hardwired to RHCP, an Amphenol Cavity Filter with a custom built [LNA-Filter-Board](https://git.dk0tu.de/afutub/famp-pcb/-/tree/rev3) and a Lime-Mini-SDR.

You can follow the stations operation live in an [asciinema-stream](https://asciinema.org/s/MsgCXmGxqg6lkLPq).

#### Quick Notes on Operations

Please mind some short remarks on the stations operation:

- Please try to leave some minutes pause between observations. _(The rotor drives into parking position, to ensure unwinding the cables.)_
- Prefer scheduling passes with a minimum culmination of 12°. _(Although the Antennas are powerful, they can not perform miracles. Please mind other fellows and do not schedule 2° or 3°, if not absolutely necessary!)_
- We enforce a fair-scheduling scheme on this station: You can freely schedule one transmitter five times. After five observations, the station will check the overall success rate for that transmitter. If it is below a threshold of 45%, it will de-schedule your observation.
- The station provides IQ-Data automatically. These can be loaded from: [https://tubcloud.tu-berlin.de/s/BwytjxFXN3dPAdB](https://tubcloud.tu-berlin.de/s/BwytjxFXN3dPAdB)

The IQ-Data comes directly from the satnogs-flowgraph. It is doppler-corrected by the observations TLE. Please mind, that we will keep the data only for a limited time due to memory constraints.

We are looking forward to see good observations. :)

Bests, have fun and vy73 de DK0TU

name: N5ZKK-UHF-HELICAL
description:
## Contact

[Libre Space Community](https://community.libre.space/u/n5zkk)

[N5ZKK satellite array](https://trolinger.com/david/satellite/)

[SatNOGS notes and TLE scripts](https://trolinger.com/david/satnogs/)

## Configuration

UHF homebrew helical (70cm, 12+ years on the roof) <-> SSB Electronic 1037 NF SP/70 <-> LMR400 superflex <-> RTL-SDR

VHF homebrew helical <-> JG-ULNA2VOX-E <-> RTL-SDR

Rotator: Yaesu G-5500 with Green Heron controller, rotctld to Windows PstRotator

PC: J1900, Ubuntu 20.x, SatNOGS compiled from source

Also on the array: cross-pol VHF/UHF yagis, 1m offset dish with 1700 MHz 3D-printed helical feed and Nooelec GOES+

When not on SatNOGS: NOAA, Meteor, MetOp, GOES with SatDump, Orbitron, PstRotator, WXtoImg

Parts and local shops: Gibsons Radio and Radio Shack, Kerrville TX

## Timeline

- 1989 first sat station: modified PRO-2006 and homemade helical on a Radio Shack rotator
- About 2006 current roof array planned and built; still in its second decade
- 2019 SatNOGS station online
- 2021 VHF helical refurbished and VHF receiver finished
- 2024-12 current array photos on the satellite page
- 2025 1700 MHz helical feed refurbished
- Now full AZ/EL when not used for POES and ham radio

## TLE

Local scripts merge Space-Track and CelesTrak, keep the newest epoch, and decode Alpha-5 catalog IDs: [satnogs-tle](https://trolinger.com/david/satnogs/satnogs-tle.txt) [crontab](https://trolinger.com/david/satnogs/crontab.txt) [satellites](https://trolinger.com/david/satnogs/satellites.txt) [merge](https://trolinger.com/david/satnogs/mergetles.txt)

name: MEGANISI_1
description:
#### About Meganisi 1
   Station in western greece, ionian islands. A minimalist setup and proof of concept for reducing e-waste.
It started as a challenge to run something useful on **an old tv-box** and has since seen a few upgrades with better antennas and better mounting locations.

| Parameter                               | Details |
| :--- | :--- |
Compute | Old X96 Mini TV-Box
OS | ARMBIAN (Amlogic)
SDR | RTL-SDR V3
LNA | RTL-SDR LNA
Antenna Materials | Aluminum
  |  


**Known Limitations:**

- Mounting point could be better. Currently there are still tree tops and buildings nearby.
- Due to the above, min horizon is rather high. Will fix in future by mounting higher still.
- The X96 is inherently noisy. But using the right USB port has mitigated it somewhat.
- Island internet is sometimes unreliable. My strategy: Cope lmao.
- PMR Inmterference in summer from multiple sources.

description:
University of Auckland satellite ground station located on the
Science Centre rooftop at the City Campus in Auckland, New Zealand.

The station provides VHF and UHF satellite reception using directional
Yagi antennas mounted on a Yaesu G5500 azimuth/elevation rotator.

VHF reception is provided by an M2 2MCP14 circularly polarized antenna
covering approximately 143-148 MHz. UHF reception is provided by a
Hi-Tec Aerials Y6U Yagi covering the 70 cm satellite band.
